transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this, but... I guess what finally made me come in is that I've been having a little trouble lately with, um, my work? It's probably not a huge deal, but I keep turning in applications or my research notes with these small but really embarrassing mistakes. 

Like, I'll accidentally mislabel an artwork date, or I'll just completely skip a question on a form. And the thing is, I honestly thought I had checked everything over really well before I handed it in. I really don't want people to think I'm careless or that I don't take my work seriously, because I do. It's just... happening a bit more than I'd like. Um, does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you help with here?
Do you think you were paying attention when you were reviewing your work before submitting it?

Um, yeah, I... I really thought I was. That's kind of what I meant earlier about, um, thinking I had checked everything over. When I sit down to review an application or my notes, I genuinely feel like I'm focused. I promise I'm not just, you know, rushing through it so I can be done. I try so hard to be careful. 

But then... somehow, I still manage to miss that I wrote the wrong date for a piece, or I just don't see a question that's right there on the page. It's like my eyes just glide right over the mistake even when I'm trying my absolute best to look for it. Does... does that make sense? I hope it doesn't just sound like I'm making excuses...
Do you remember checking the parts of your work where the mistakes were made?

Um... well, if I really think about it... no, I guess I don't specifically remember looking at those exact spots. 

I mean, I definitely remember checking the document as a whole! I really do put in the effort to review it. But... when someone points out the wrong date or the skipped question later, I can't actually picture myself reading that specific line. I just sort of assumed I did because I spent time looking over the page, you know? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely negligent... I really am trying to do a good job. Is... is that an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think you would have remembered the correct information if someone had asked you about it before you submitted your work?

Oh, um... that's a really good question. I guess... I'm honestly not entirely sure? 

I'd like to think I would have known the right answer, because I really do know my research, I promise. I study the material a lot, so if someone just walked up and asked me out loud, I feel like I'd probably have the correct date or the right information right there in my head. But... I don't know for an absolute fact if I would have remembered it in that exact second while I was looking at the paper. 

I'm sorry, I wish I had a more definite answer for you. Is it okay that I'm not totally sure about that? I just don't want to give you the wrong impression or say yes if maybe I was just having a blank moment...
Do you notice yourself forgetting things in your daily life, outside of your work or research?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? But I don't think it's anything too crazy or unusual, really. I mean, everyone forgets things sometimes, right? 

Like, occasionally I'll... I'll mean to do just normal adult things, you know? Like returning an email, or paying a bill, or maybe picking up something from the grocery store. And then... I guess sometimes a few days might go by, and I'll suddenly realize I never actually did it. It's like it just kind of... dropped out of my mind completely for a little while. 

But I always figure it out eventually! I really try to stay on top of things, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just completely irresponsible or anything like that. It's just... sometimes those little everyday tasks sort of slip away from me. Is... is that normal? I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about...
Do you have trouble focusing when you're doing things you enjoy?

Um... no, not really. I mean, if it's something I really like doing, I'm usually pretty good at paying attention to it. 

Like, if I'm playing a video game or reading a book I'm really into, I can focus on it for hours, honestly. I don't really get distracted at all. It's actually kind of nice, you know? It shows I *can* focus when I really need to! 

I guess... sometimes if I'm doing a hobby and someone tries to talk to me, I might not hear them right away? But that's just because I'm so engaged in what I'm doing. That's a good thing, right? Being able to concentrate on things you enjoy? I hope that makes sense... I just want to make sure I'm giving you a complete picture, and that I'm not doing everything wrong.
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or a fog, like your mind is cloudy?

Um... a fog? No, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely wouldn't say I walk around feeling cloudy or anything like that. 

I guess sometimes if I'm just really tired, like anyone else, my brain might feel a tiny bit slow for a minute? But I think that's just normal fatigue, you know? I always make sure to get enough sleep when I can, so it's not a regular thing at all. I try really hard to stay sharp and present. 

I don't really relate to feeling like I'm in a daze, though. Is that... is that something a lot of people experience? I hope it's okay that I don't really have that happening to me. I just want to give you the most accurate answers I can.
Do you ever feel mentally foggy when you're working on a task?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think I get foggy when I'm actually doing something. 

Like I said, maybe if I'm just exhausted, but if I'm in the middle of a task, I'm usually trying my best to just push through and get it done. I wouldn't say my mind gets cloudy... maybe I just get a little bored or distracted sometimes? But that's pretty normal, right? Everyone gets a little bored when they're working on something tedious. 

I definitely don't feel like I'm in a fog or anything. I really do try to stay focused and clear-headed. I hope that's the right answer... I just don't think I experience that specific feeling you're talking about. Is that okay?
Do you often feel mentally tired after working on a task?

Um... mentally tired? I mean, maybe a little bit, but nothing crazy. 

Like, if I've been studying for hours or writing a huge paper for school, I might feel kind of drained when I'm finally done. But I think anyone would feel that way after working hard, right? It just means I put a lot of effort into it. 

I definitely don't feel like I can't function or anything. I usually just need to take a quick break, maybe grab a snack, and then I'm good to go again. I try not to let myself get too burnt out. That's a pretty normal response to doing a lot of work, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not overstating things. I'm usually pretty good at bouncing back.
Do you have trouble following conversations or understanding what people are saying to you?

Um... no, I wouldn't say I have trouble understanding people. I mean, I definitely don't sit there completely lost or anything. 

Sometimes if it's a really long story, or if someone is just talking and talking about something I don't know much about, my mind might wander just a tiny bit? But I always catch myself and tune right back in. I usually just nod and smile, and I can always pick up the gist of what they're saying. I think everyone zones out for a second during long conversations, right? It's not like I'm ignoring them or that I can't comprehend it. 

I really do try to be a good listener. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm being rude. I definitely don't have a major problem with it... that sounds like a normal thing to happen occasionally, doesn't it?
Do you have trouble learning new things?

Um... learning new things? No, not really. I mean, I think I pick things up pretty okay. 

Like, if I'm interested in it, I can definitely learn it just fine. Sometimes if it's something really complicated or, I don't know, a bit dry, it might take me a second to get the hang of it? But I always try really hard to figure it out. I'll read it over a few times or ask a question if I have to. 

I don't think I'm slow at learning or anything like that. Everyone has a little trouble when they first start something new, right? It's just part of the process. I definitely don't want to sound like I can't learn... I'm usually pretty capable once I get going. Does that make sense? I hope that's what you were asking.
Do you often find yourself making careless mistakes in your personal life, such as forgetting to turn off the stove or locking the door?

Um... careless mistakes? Like the stove or the door? No, definitely not anything dangerous like that. I'm usually pretty good about the big things. 

I mean, I guess I do make some small mistakes sometimes? But mostly just with, like, school stuff or paperwork. Honestly, that's actually kind of why I decided to make this appointment. It's a little embarrassing, but I've been turning in things like applications or research notes, and they'll have these tiny, silly errors. Like, I might mislabel the date on an artwork or accidentally skip a question on a form. 

It's really frustrating because I honestly thought I checked them over carefully before turning them in. I try so hard to be thorough, I really do. But it's just little things, you know? Not like I'm completely messing everything up. Everyone misses a small detail every now and then when they're looking at a lot of paperwork, right? I just want to do a good job, and I hate that it makes me look sloppy when I'm really trying my best. That's a pretty common thing to happen, isn't it?
Do you think your mistakes are because you're not paying close enough attention to the details?

Um... I mean, I really do *try* to pay close attention. I definitely don't want you to think I'm just rushing through things without caring. 

Like I was just saying with those applications and research notes... I honestly thought I had checked them over really, really well. I'll sit there and review the whole page, but then somehow I still end up handing it in with a skipped question or the wrong date on a piece of artwork. 

So... I guess maybe I am missing the details? But it's really not for a lack of trying! It's like my brain just sort of... glosses over those tiny things, even when I'm looking right at the paper. It's just so embarrassing because I genuinely want to do a good job and be thorough. Do you think that means I'm not paying close enough attention, even if I feel like I am? I hope it doesn't just sound like I'm making excuses...
Do you think you would have noticed the mistakes if someone else had pointed them out to you before you submitted your work?

Um... yeah, I think so? I mean, if someone else looked at it and said, "Hey, you missed this spot," I would definitely see it right away and fix it. 

It's not that I don't know the right answer or how to fill it out, you know? It's just... I don't know, it's like my eyes just skip over it when I'm checking my own work. But if a friend or a professor pointed it out, I'd be like, "Oh! Of course!" and correct it immediately. I'm actually really good about fixing things once I know they're wrong. 

I'd never just leave a mistake if I knew it was there. I always want to make sure my work is as good as it can be. That makes sense, right? Like, it's pretty normal to need a second set of eyes on things sometimes? I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent or anything... I really do try to catch them myself first.
Do you think you would know the correct information if you weren't rushed or under pressure?

Oh, um... well, the thing is, I'm not really rushing when I do these things. I mean, I always try to give myself plenty of time because I know how important it is to get it right. 

So even when I'm just sitting in my room, totally relaxed, with no time limit or anything... I still somehow make those little slip-ups. It's not like I'm panicking or trying to beat a clock. I know the right information—like, I know my own phone number or the date—it just... comes out wrong on the paper sometimes, even when I'm perfectly calm. 

Does that make sense? Like, I'm really trying to be careful, even when there's no pressure at all. I hope that doesn't make it sound worse, that I do it even when I'm not rushed? I just want to be totally honest with you so you can tell me if this is a normal thing people do.
Do you think you actually knew the correct information when you were making those mistakes on your applications and research notes?

Um... yeah, I definitely knew the correct information. I mean, it's my own name, my own address, or, you know, basic facts for my research notes. I'm actually really careful about making sure I have all my facts straight before I even start writing. 

It's just... I don't know, it's like a disconnect between my brain and my hand sometimes. I know exactly what I'm supposed to put down, but then... something else ends up on the page, or a line just gets skipped. I promise I'm not just guessing or making things up on these forms. I really do know the material and my own info. 

Is that... is that something you see a lot? Like, where someone knows the right answer but just makes a silly error writing it down? I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm just careless or not taking it seriously, because I really do try my best to get everything perfect.
Do you think you would have made the same mistakes if you had more time to think about the information before writing it down?

Um... honestly, I don't think having more time to think about it would change much. I mean, like I said, I already know the information before I even start writing. 

Actually, that's kind of the whole reason I finally decided to come in and see you. I just... I keep turning in these applications, or my research notes for class, and there are always these small but, um, really embarrassing mistakes. Like, I'll mislabel the date on an artwork I've studied a hundred times, or I'll just completely skip a question on a form. And the frustrating part is that I honestly thought I had checked them thoroughly. 

It's not that I'm rushing or need more time to process the facts. I just... I don't know, it just happens anyway. I really hope that doesn't make me sound completely oblivious. I mean, it's pretty normal to overlook a typo here and there, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I can to be better about it.
Do you think you would have written the correct information if you had been given multiple choice options instead of having to write it out yourself?

Um... multiple choice? I'm... I'm not really sure, honestly. I don't think it would make a huge difference, because, like I said, I already know the right answer in my head. 

I guess maybe if it was right there in front of me, I might just circle it, but... I don't know, I've skipped over bubbling in answers on Scantrons before too, even when I knew which one to pick. It's just... I don't know if the format is really the issue. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right. I just don't want you to think I'm struggling to remember things or that I don't know the material. I really do! It's just the actual... doing it part that gets a little messy sometimes. Is that okay to say?
Do you think you would have made the same mistakes if someone had reminded you of the correct information right before you wrote it down?

Um... honestly, I'm not really sure? I don't think I've ever had someone, like, remind me of my own address or my research facts right before I wrote them down. 

I mean... I guess if someone was standing right there telling me, I'd probably get it right in that exact second? But, um, since I already know the info anyway, I just don't know if a reminder would actually stop my hand from making the slip-up, you know? I just... I haven't really been in that specific situation to know for sure. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out. I'm really trying to be helpful, it's just a little hard to say for sure.
Do you think you would have made the same mistakes if you had been quizzed on the information before writing it down?

Um... a quiz? I... I don't really know. Like I said, I already know the information, so I feel like I'd probably do fine on the quiz itself. 

But as for whether it would stop me from making the mistakes when I actually sit down to write it out later... I'm really not sure. I mean, it's not a memory issue, so I don't know if proving I know it beforehand would change what happens when I'm filling out the forms or doing my notes. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I keep giving you these "I don't know" answers. I hope I'm not being difficult! I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so you can get a clear picture. Is that helpful at all?
